alex: Nightly eval alert — quantized-v2 job spike: 24% prompt failures, mostly timeouts and 'bad_generation' on long-context prompts. Pasting short log.

 eval-bot: nightly-run 1954320000 finished: 85 passed, 27 failed. See /runs/1954320000

 mina: Do we have a repro? Any infra changes rolled yesterday?

 alex: Rolled a small perf hotfix (prefetch-tokenizer-cache) to staging -> prod yesterday evening. It changes tokenizer cache serialization and writes temp files under /var/tmp/tokenizer_cache_{pid}. It was supposed to be no-op.

 raj: Can you paste a minimal failing prompt + the exact command to reproduce locally?

 alex: Sure — repro below. It only fails under quantized model and when promptset is zstd-compressed. Note use of TOKENIZER_CACHE=/var/tmp/tokenizer_cache_{pid}

 ```bash
 # repro (ran inside docker:cpu-quant)
 python -m eval_harness.run \n   --model redwood/quantized-v2 \n   --promptset data/promptsets/long_dialogs.jsonl.zst \n   --batch 1 --workers 4 \n   --tokenizer-cache /var/tmp/tokenizer_cache_$RANDOM
 ```

 and snippet from worker log:
 ```
 E 12:03:21 tokenizer_cache.py:write_cache: failed mkstemp('/var/tmp/tokenizer_cache_1234.tmp'): File exists
 W 12:03:21 tokenizer_cache.py:write_cache: fallback to open with mode 'w'
 E 12:03:21 zstd: DecompressionError: Unexpected end of stream
 E 12:03:21 worker.py:main: worker exiting due to decompress error
 ```

 mina: Huh — mkstemp returning EEXIST is odd (mkstemp should fail if exists). Sounds like there is a race where multiple workers try to create the same temp name. Where is the temp name coming from? pid-based -> collisions possible inside container reused pids.

 alex: Agreed. strace from a failing run shows rapid sequence: one worker creates tmp, writes, then another tries mkstemp with same name while the file is still being moved/renamed by writer -> second sees EEXIST and falls back to non-atomic write which corrupts zstd blob.

 raj: Fix ideas:
 - use mkstemp with guaranteed unique name (include uuid) or tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)
 - write to temp -> fsync -> os.replace for atomic rename
 - coordinate with flock for concurrent writers
 Also quick test: run with TOKENIZER_CACHE_DISABLE=1 — if that removes failures it's a strong signal.

 alex: Ran TOKENIZER_CACHE_DISABLE=1 locally and a full nightly run completed with 0 failures. Will open PR to switch to atomic rename + uuid in temp name and add integration test that starts 8 worker processes against a zst promptset.

 ops-sre: Rolling back prod deploy now (in 3 min) and will keep staging disabled for the hotfix. Please add rollback notes and the PR link.

 alex: Will do. PR + test will include reproducer and a small stress.sh that spawns 12 workers. Thanks :thumbsup:
